lead: Indianapolis has cold winters, hard water, basements and old brick neighborhoods. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across the city.
risk: frozen pipes, basement sewer backups and hard water scale
risk_short: frozen pipes, sewer backups and hard water
why: Irvington, Fountain Square and Meridian-Kessler have many homes from the early 1900s. They often have old steel supply pipes, cast-iron stacks and clay sewer lines.
Older parts of the city drain to combined sewers. In heavy rain, these can back up into basements. Winter cold freezes pipes near outside walls and in crawl spaces.
water: Citizens Energy Group supplies the city from the White River, Fall Creek, local reservoirs and wells. The water is hard. Scale builds up in water heaters and on fixtures.
problems: Irvington, Fountain Square and older areas
tips: Add a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Flush your water heater each year.
Test your sump pump each spring.
areas: PipeMend works in Broad Ripple, Fountain Square, Irvington, Mass Ave and every other part of town.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the city's Department of Business and Neighborhood Services. Plumbers must be licensed by the Indiana Plumbing Commission.

faq.q: Why do Indianapolis basements back up?
faq.a: Older parts of the city have combined sewers that carry rain and wastewater together. In big storms they fill up and push water back through floor drains. A backwater valve helps protect the basement.
